angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 40,230,244 km at 44.74 pc = 12.02 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 89642: distance 44.743 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.011), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 44.743 +/- 0.492 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 23.8859 +/- 0.4865 mas (same row, RUWE 1.51), 49.1 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 57.827 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 89642: radius 57.827 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 526.257 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.07) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 40,230,244 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 3638 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 89642: effective temperature 3638 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.2) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 89642: effective temperature 3638 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.2) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)
spectralTypeSource: SIMBAD, * eta Sgr: spectral type M2III (1982MSS...C03....0H)
